ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To chew over is to find material for conceptual working, verbal rumination, or sustained investigation.
EvidenceBody: Chan records extend the bodily action to sayings and public cases: Yunxi Langting Ting tells beginners to “chew over a ready-made sentence that cannot be knocked down” and repeats “chew it over, chew it over” (咬嚼來、咬嚼去); the same record says Wujin spent his whole life unable to chew through “the bowl-carrying public case” (托缽公案). Other comments use the resistance of food as an explicit comparison: a saying can be “unable to be chewed through” (咬嚼不破), while Donglin offers only “wooden-slat soup and iron-nail rice—chew as you will” (木札羹、鉄釘飯，任汝咬嚼). The record also issues the opposite verdict, “strictly avoid chewing” (切忌咬嚼), after the answer “a thousand-year peach pit.”
